200.title: Polish president reappoints General Wieslaw Kukula as army chief
200.summary: Polish president reappoints General Wieslaw Kukula as army chief President Karol Nawrocki has reappointed General Wieslaw Kukula for another term as Chief of the General Staff of the Polish Armed Forces, the National Security Bureau (BBN) announced on Tuesday.
200.body: Polish president reappoints General Wieslaw Kukula as army chief President Karol Nawrocki has reappointed General Wieslaw Kukula for another term as Chief of the General Staff of the Polish Armed Forces, the National Security Bureau (BBN) announced on Tuesday. 06.10.2026 12:33 update: 06.10.2026 12:34 Photo: PAP/Albert Zawada BBN head Bartosz Grodecki wrote on X that the appointment will take effect on October 10, marking the end of Kukula's first three-year term. Under Poland's Homeland Defence Act, the term of office for the chief of the General Staff and branch commanders is three years, with the possibility of reappointment. General Kukula was originally appointed as the country's highest-ranking military officer on October 10, 2023. (PAP) mmr/aj

400.title: Poland delays start of first nuclear reactor to 2036 in updated programme
400.summary: Poland has adopted an updated version of its nuclear programme that pushes back the timeline for its first plant. Other nuclear announcements have been made internationally, such as the 690 MW nuclear agreement between Constellation and Amazon at Calvert Cliffs or the nuclear AI agreement signed by NANO Nuclear, IP3 and Cybernetic Intelligence.
400.body: Poland has adopted an updated version of its nuclear programme that pushes back the timeline for its first plant. Other nuclear announcements have been made internationally, such as the 690 MW nuclear agreement between Constellation and Amazon at Calvert Cliffs or the nuclear AI agreement signed by NANO Nuclear, IP3 and Cybernetic Intelligence. The initial schedule provided for construction of the first plant to start in 2026 and for the first reactor, of 1.0-1.6 GWe, to be commissioned in 2033. Content of the updated programme The updated programme provides for the construction of two nuclear power plants with a total capacity of up to 9 GWe.
